messages:
Lena: quick RFC follow-up: propose we move retry decisioning entirely into the transport layer and make paginator/iterator objects strictly mechanical (fetch(cursor) -> items). goal: reduce surprises when retries + pagination interact.
Omar: makes sense from a separation-of-concerns POV. iterator should not implicitly retry across page boundaries because it hides partial progress and can duplicate work.
Priya: agree but UX question: most users expect "for item in client.list()" to be resilient. if transport swallows errors, we need well-defined semantics for idempotency and visibility into retries.
Sam: what about long-running generators? if transport retries across pages, we need a way to signal that an iterator resumed mid-stream vs restarted the page. otherwise app-level checkpointing is hard.
Lena: idea: transport offers two modes: conservative (retry only on transient within a single page fetch, fail on cursor-related errors) and aggressive (retry across page boundaries with de-dupe tokens). default = conservative.
Omar: conservative default seems safer. Implementation options:
- SDK-level: implement retry wrapper around the HTTP/gRPC call. paginator sits on top unchanged.
- Runtime-level: expose a RetryPolicy to control cross-page behavior and inject a dedupe token header when allowed.
Priya: dedupe header is neat but requires server-side support. not all models/endpoints will honor it. fallback: client could use per-page resume tokens we accept as opaque and avoid re-fetching exact IDs.
Sam: ergonomics for Python/TS/Go: keep paginator API identical:
```py
# python sketch
for item in client.list_things(page_size=100):
    process(item)
```
But add optional transport config: client = RedwoodClient(retries_on_page_boundary='aggressive')
```ts
// ts sketch
const c = new RedwoodClient({ retries: { mode: 'conservative' } });
for await (const item of c.listThings()) { ... }
```
Lena: important: telemetry + observability. each page fetch should emit a page_event (cursor_present:bool, attempt_count:int, final_status:string). don't leak cursor contents.
Omar: agree on privacy. hashed_cursor or cursor_present flag only. Also emit an idempotency_token if transport used one so server ops can correlate. token should be short-lived and not stored.
Priya: backwards compat: older SDKs will keep current behaviour (best-effort retries). new SDKs should default to conservative. document migration path and add lint warning in changelog.
Sam: testing strategy: unit tests around duplicate suppression, integration tests against a staging server that simulates flaky pages and returns duplicate items when re-requested. should also include perf test to see tail-latency impact.
deploy-bot: checklist: add feature flag retry-mode + telemetry toggle, run canary at 2% for 48h, monitor item-duplication rate and error-surface.
Lena: ops plan: if duplication > 0.1% in canary, roll back aggressive mode and keep conservative. also capture user-facing error-rate increase.
Omar: edge case: streaming endpoints (server-streamed tokens) are different; we should not apply cross-page aggressive retries there. mark streaming as opt-out.
Priya: i will draft the RFC addendum with API sketches, telemetry schema, canary plan and a migration checklist. tagging @Sam for integration test ownership.
Sam: will add test harness and a small reference implementation in the go sdk.
Lena: thanks all. i'll open the RFC PR with the above and include a short example migration guide for customers. :white_check_mark:
